title: COEP, CORP and nested frame navigations
body:
At https://mikewest.github.io/corpp/#corp-check, we have the following steps.

1. Set embedder policy to "unsafe-none" if both of the following statements are true:
   1. request’s client's embedder policy is "unsafe-none".
   1. request’s reserved client is not null, and its embedder policy is "unsafe-none".
1. Return allowed if any of the following statements are true:
   1. request’s mode is "same-origin", "cors", or "websocket".
   1. request’s mode is "navigate", and embedder policy is "unsafe-none".

I talked with @mikewest a bit, and it seems what we want to achieve is having the CORP check for all nested frame navigations. So I think the following steps are easier to understand (assuming we have https://github.com/whatwg/fetch/pull/948):

1. Return allowed if any of the following statements are true:
   1. request’s mode is "same-origin", "cors", or "websocket".
   1. request’s mode is "navigate" and request's destination is "document" __[edited]__.
   1. request’s mode is "navigate" and request’s client's embedder policy is "unsafe-none".

I wrote some tests (with impl) at https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/2066358/2.

But we have another problem I think: the origin we use for the CORP check is coming from the navigation source, not the parent frame.

Let's say we have a top-level frame T of origin A, nested frame N of origin B in it. T has COEP: require-corp, N has COEP: require-corp and CORP: cross-origin. When a navigation happens in N, the navigation request's origin is B, not A. So, A/x.html (COEP: require-corp, CORP: same-origin) is rejected while B/y.html (COEP: require-corp, CORP: same-origin) is allowed. I feel it confusing...

We have some options:
1. Drop this feature (i.e., CORP works only for "no-cors" requests).
1. Keep the behavior I described above.
1. Have a mechanism to check the same-originness with the parent frame's origin. I can think of several ways...
   1. Have a separate property in request and have the CORP check use that origin for navigation.
   1. Add a parameter in the COEP header; something like embedded-as=(same-origin/same-site/cross-origin), and check that in [the navigation response processing](https://mikewest.github.io/corpp/#process-navigation-response) (This means CORP works only for "no-cors" requests).
   1. Run the CORP check in [the navigation response processing](https://mikewest.github.io/corpp/#process-navigation-response) with a custom origin.
   1. Introduce another HTTP header, and check that in [the navigation response processing](https://mikewest.github.io/corpp/#process-navigation-response) (This means CORP works only for "no-cors" requests).

I prefer 1 or 3.ii. What we want to check seems different from CORP.

@mikewest @annevk what do you think?
